description: Hi! I’m Bansari, an 8th-grade student passionate about Earth science, space weather, and the Moon. I'm building a NASA Space Apps team to tackle fun challenges and create something about rising sea levels. Whether you code, design, or love space, let's team up and build something amazing! I would love if you join! 😆
summary:
Sea Level Detective is a visual data-storytelling presentation that investigates how global mean sea level has changed from 1993 to the present using official NASA satellite altimetry observations.
To address the "Be An Earth System Trend Detective!" challenge, this project breaks down how radar satellites measure ocean surface height from space, analyzes over three decades of NASA sea-level records to reveal a clear upward trend despite seasonal fluctuations, and explains the two main scientific drivers behind the rise: warming seawater expansion and melting land ice.
Raw climate data can often feel overwhelming to students and everyday citizens. By turning complex NASA observations into a clear, step-by-step visual investigation, this project helps local communities and young learners easily understand real-world ocean trends and why protecting our planet matters.
details:
What It Does & How It Works:
Sea Level Detective is a 7-slide visual science investigation that explains how global mean sea level has changed from 1993 to the present using official NASA satellite data. It guides readers through three clear steps:

  1. How Satellites Measure Oceans: Explains radar altimetry—how satellites send radar pulses to the ocean surface, measure the return travel time, and calculate sea-surface height.
  2. Analyzing the Evidence (1993–Present): Presents NASA’s Global Mean Sea Level graph to show both short-term seasonal ups and downs and the long-term upward trend of over 100 mm.
  3. Understanding the Causes: Breaks down the two main reasons sea levels are rising: thermal expansion (warmer water takes up more space) and melting land ice (glaciers and ice sheets adding water to the ocean).
  4. Benefits & Intended Impact:
    Climate graphs and raw satellite data can be hard for students and everyday people to understand. By turning NASA data into a visual "detective" story, this project makes climate evidence easy to read and empowers students and local communities to learn how our oceans are changing and why protecting our planet matters.

Tools & Software Used:

  • NASA Sea Level Change Portal: Official Global Mean Sea Level (GMSL) satellite altimetry dataset and time-series chart (1993–present).
  • Google Slides: Used to design, organize, and present the visual investigation on a Chromebook.
  • Creativity & Key Factors Considered:
    To make the science engaging for learners of all ages, I framed the presentation as a "detective mission" with clear step-by-step clues, simple diagrams, and bold visual contrasts. When designing the slides, I focused on accuracy (using real NASA observations), clarity (avoiding overly complicated jargon), and visual storytelling so anyone can understand the trend in just a few minutes.
